title: Trade
tagline: The meaning and forms of trade, the channels goods move through, and the middlemen who make the channel work. Unit weight: 10 marks.

overview.intro: Trade is the purchase and sale of goods and services with the object of earning profit, and it is the final link between the maker and the user. Without trade, a weaver would have to find and persuade every buyer personally; with trade, wholesalers, retailers and agents absorb the difference between mass production and individual consumption. This unit defines trade and its forms, examines internal and external trade, sets out the channels through which goods reach the consumer, and classifies the middlemen who operate in those channels by function rather than by name.

learningOutcomes: Define trade and state its importance.

Describe the channels of distribution available to a producer.

learn.title: Meaning, importance and forms of trade

blocks.text: Trade is the activity of buying and selling goods and services, and it exists because production and consumption are separated in place, time, quantity and possession. A rice farmer produces tonnes in one season while a household buys kilograms every month, and that gap must be bridged before anyone can eat. Trade bridges it by creating possession utility, moving ownership from the person who has surplus to the person who wants it, and it does so repeatedly and with the intention of profit.

blocks.text: A channel is the path a product follows to reach its buyer. The shortest is the direct channel, where the producer sells to the consumer through her own shop or website, which gives maximum control and the full margin but demands capital in outlets and delivery. The longer channels insert middlemen: producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer is the standard pattern for physical consumer goods, while producer to retailer to consumer suits large or perishable items where a wholesaler adds no value.

blocks.caption: Channels available to a producer
rows: Perishable farm produce, industrial goods needing installation, online sales
Large or bulky items, garments, electronics
Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
Fast-moving consumer goods with wide distribution
Producer to agent to wholesaler to retailer
Goods entering distant or overseas markets

blocks.text: The choice depends on the density of buyers, the perishability and value of the product, the need for service after the sale, and the capital the producer can commit to distribution. A firm selling to a thousand scattered villages will use intermediaries; a firm selling machinery to fifty factories can sell directly.

items.text: Fresh milk sold by a dairy directly to households each morning.
items.note: Perishability and daily frequency make a short channel cheaper than any intermediary.

items.text: Packaged biscuits distributed through agents, wholesalers and thousands of retail outlets.
items.note: High volume and dispersed buyers justify the cost of two intermediary levels.

blocks.text: Middlemen are the traders who stand between the original producer and the final consumer, and they are classified by two questions: do they take title to the goods, and do they buy for resale or only to bring the parties together. A wholesaler and a retailer both buy and sell, so both take title and both are merchant middlemen. A broker, a commission agent and an auctioneer only bring parties together, take no title, and earn a commission, so they are functional or facilitating middlemen.

blocks.caption: Classification of middlemen
rows: Bulk purchase, bulk breaking, storage, finance to retailers
Sells in small quantities to the final consumer
Brings buyer and seller together and negotiates
Sells on behalf of a principal at the best price
Carries goods and sells door to door
Conducts sale to the highest bidder

blocks.text: The distinction matters commercially. A merchant middleman bears the risk of ownership and therefore needs a margin, while a facilitating middleman earns only a fee and carries no inventory risk. A producer who uses a broker keeps more control and pays less, but loses the credit and storage functions a wholesaler would have provided.

learn.title: Services performed by wholesalers and retailers

blocks.text: Wholesalers perform functions no producer wants to perform at scale: they buy in bulk, which lets the producer manufacture in long runs; they break bulk into the smaller lots retailers can handle; they store goods until needed, creating time utility; they finance retailers by extending credit; and they bear the risk of inventory and collection. Retailers perform the final functions: they assort goods from many producers into one place, provide the convenience of location and hours, offer credit and delivery to regular customers, and give the producer feedback about what is actually selling.

items.note: Bulk breaking lets fifty retailers hold stock they could never buy in full truckloads.

items.note: Assortment saves the customer from visiting every producer separately.

keyPoints: Trade is buying and selling for profit, closing the gap between production and consumption.
It bridges separation in place, time, quantity and possession.
Wholesale trade deals in bulk for resale; retail trade sells small quantities to the consumer.
Internal trade stays within the country; external trade crosses borders.
Channels may be direct or indirect with one, two or three intermediary levels.
The channel choice depends on product, market density, service need and available capital.
Merchant middlemen take title and bear risk; facilitating middlemen do not.
Wholesalers break bulk, store, finance retailers and bear inventory risk.
Retailers assort, provide convenience, give service and pass back demand information.
Every intermediary earns from the function performed, not from the transaction alone.
examFocus: Ten marks supports a full channel question: draw or name the channel, then justify the choice for the product given.
Middlemen classification must turn on title and function, which is the distinction examiners look for.
Services questions expect separate lists for wholesalers and retailers, not a combined paragraph.

questions.prompt: The essential difference between wholesale and retail trade is:
options: Wholesale sells to consumers while retail sells to traders
Wholesale sells in bulk for resale while retail sells small quantities for final consumption
Wholesale never takes title while retail does
Wholesale operates abroad and retail at home
questions.answer: Wholesale sells in bulk for resale while retail sells small quantities for final consumption
questions.explanation: The distinction rests on quantity and on the purpose of purchase, since the wholesaler buys for resale and the retailer for final consumption.

questions.prompt: A broker who brings a buyer and a seller together without owning the goods is a:
questions.explanation: Because no title passes, the broker performs only the function of matching the parties and earns a commission.

questions.prompt: Which channel suits packaged soaps sold through thousands of villages?
options: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
questions.answer: Producer to wholesaler to retailer to consumer
questions.explanation: High volume with widely dispersed retail points justifies a wholesaler who breaks bulk and reaches small outlets the producer could not service economically.

questions.prompt: The function of a wholesaler that most directly enables a manufacturer to plan long production runs is:
questions.explanation: Buying in large quantities removes the need for the manufacturer to find many small buyers, so production can be scheduled in long uninterrupted runs.

questions.prompt: The trade that takes place within the boundaries of one country is called __________ trade.
questions.explanation: Internal or home trade stays inside the country, while external trade crosses national borders into import, export or entrepot trade.

questions.prompt: The route that goods follow from the producer to the final consumer is known as the channel of __________ .
questions.explanation: The channel may be direct or may insert intermediaries, and its length depends on the product and the market.

questions.prompt: State four services performed by wholesalers to producers.
questions.answer: Four services are: they buy the output in bulk, which lets the producer manufacture in long runs; they break bulk into the smaller quantities retailers can handle; they store goods until retailers need them, creating time utility; and they finance retailers by extending credit, which shortens the producer’s own collection period. Bearing the risk of stock and bad debts is also accepted.
questions.explanation: Each service must show how it helps the producer or the channel, not merely what the wholesaler does.

questions.prompt: Distinguish between merchant middlemen and facilitating middlemen.
questions.answer: A merchant middleman buys the goods and takes title to them, so he owns the stock, bears the risk of price and collection, and earns a margin on resale; wholesalers, retailers and hawkers belong to this group. A facilitating middleman only brings the buyer and the seller together or performs a supporting service, never takes title, and earns a commission or fee; brokers, commission agents and auctioneers belong here. The distinction therefore turns on whether ownership passes through the middleman.
questions.explanation: The test of title must be stated explicitly, since that is the criterion that separates the two groups.

questions.prompt: Explain the functions performed by retailers in a channel of distribution.
questions.answer: Retailers perform the functions that bring a producer’s output to the individual buyer. They assort goods from many producers into a single place, so the customer can satisfy a whole need without visiting each maker. They provide convenience of location, opening hours, credit and delivery, which is what the customer actually pays a margin for. They offer personal service, demonstration and advice, which reduce the buyer’s uncertainty and the producer’s need to explain the product at every point of sale. They bear the small quantity risk and hold stock close to the point of consumption, which shortens the producer’s own distribution cycle. Finally they collect and pass back information about what is selling, what is priced wrongly and what competitors are doing, which is a service to production planning as much as to selling.
questions.explanation: Full marks need at least four distinct functions with the benefit of each named, plus the feedback function which weaker answers omit.

questions.prompt: A jam manufacturer sells only through her own shop in one town and wants national reach without building a sales force. Recommend a channel, name the middlemen you would use, and state what each would contribute and what the manufacturer would give up.
questions.answer: The recommended channel is producer to agent to wholesaler to retailer to consumer, which is the three-level channel designed for reaching scattered markets without a direct sales force. The agent would open the market in each region, taking orders and locating wholesalers and carrying no inventory, earning a commission, which keeps the manufacturer’s fixed cost low. The wholesaler would buy in truckloads, break bulk into cases, hold stock locally, finance retailers through credit and bear the collection risk, contributing storage and credit that the manufacturer would otherwise have to fund herself. The retailer would give the product shelf space, display and proximity to the buyer, and would pass back demand information. What the manufacturer gives up is control over price and presentation at the point of sale, a substantial part of the margin as each intermediary earns for its function, and direct contact with the consumer, which means feedback arrives filtered through two layers. She should therefore protect the brand by setting a recommended price, insist on agreed display standards in the agreement, and read the retail-level data the wholesaler supplies, so that national reach is gained without losing the ability to correct the market.
questions.explanation: The answer earns marks for choosing the right channel, attributing a specific contribution to each middleman, and stating honestly what control is surrendered.
